21	## 1. Context — Why This Matters
22	
23	Karpathy released a tiny open-source framework called `autoresearch`. The idea is dead simple:
24	
25	> Let an AI agent **change one file**, **run a test**, **score the result**, then **keep the change or throw it away** — and repeat that loop overnight without you babysitting it.
26	
27	He built it for ML training runs. But the **pattern itself** — *modify → score → keep-or-revert → repeat* — works anywhere you can measure quality.
28	
29	Content Hub V2 has 10 prompts that were written once and never tested systematically. Every video script, hook, and title is generated by prompts nobody has measured. That's a huge improvement opportunity hiding in plain sight.
30	
31	This document is a **survey** of 5 places autoresearch fits your system, with effort/value ratings, an honest "fact vs. assumption" split for each, and concrete file-by-file mapping.
32	
33	---
34	
35	## 2. How autoresearch Works (in 30 seconds, layman terms)
36	
37	Imagine you have a recipe and a way to score the cake it produces (1-10 from a taste tester). autoresearch is the kitchen robot that:
38	
39	1. Tweaks one ingredient in the recipe.
40	2. Bakes the cake (fixed time, fixed oven settings — same every run).
41	3. Scores it.
42	4. If the score went up, **keeps the tweak.** If it went down, **rips it out.**
43	5. Tweaks something else. Repeats all night.
44	
45	In Karpathy's repo:
46	- **The recipe** = `train.py` (the only file the agent can touch)
47	- **The oven** = `prepare.py` (fixed — agent cannot change)
48	- **The taste tester** = a number called `val_bpb`
49	- **The rulebook** = `program.md` (you write this before bedtime: "tonight, optimize for X")
50	
51	**Three things make the pattern work:** one mutable file, one fixed metric, one rulebook.
52	
53	---
54	
55	## 3. Karpathy's Four Files → Our Four Files (Direct Mapping)
56	
57	The same four-file pattern, ported to Content Hub V2. Using `prompts/hook.md` as the running example — **the same shape applies to all 8 skills** (called out explicitly in each section).
58	
59	---
60	
61	### 3.1 Karpathy's `train.py`  →  our `prompts/<skill>.md`
62	
63	**Karpathy's version:** PyTorch model + optimizer + training loop. The only file the agent is allowed to mutate.
64	
65	**Our version:** the prompt markdown file. The only file `/prompt-lab` is allowed to mutate.
66	
67	**Applies to all 8 skills:** [[researcher]], [[ideation]], [[hook]], [[outline]], [[title]], [[cascade]], [[short-form]], [[voice-cleanup]].
68	
69	**Status:** all 8 files already exist on disk in `prompts/`.
70	
71	**What's inside `prompts/hook.md` today (excerpt):**
72	> *"Generate 5 Kallaway hook variations using the 3-stage structure: scroll stop, curiosity gap, payoff promise. For each hook, produce a Spoken Line, a Visual Anchor, and a Curiosity Gap Marker..."*
73	
74	**What `/prompt-lab` does to it each iteration:** rewrites sections, deletes lines, adds rules, restructures examples. Every variant gets a git commit. Bad variants → reverted. Good variants → kept and built on.
75	
76	---
77	
78	### 3.2 Karpathy's `prepare.py`  →  our `prompt-lab/fixtures/<skill>_test_topics.json` + existing `skills/<skill>.py`
79	
80	**Karpathy's version:** loads dataset, sets constants (`MAX_SEQ_LEN`, `TIME_BUDGET`, `VOCAB_SIZE`). Fixed — agent cannot touch.
81	
82	**Our version:** fixed test inputs + the skill runner. Two files together. Fixed — `/prompt-lab` cannot touch.
83	
84	**Applies to all 8 skills.** Each gets its own fixtures file paired with its own existing runner:
85	
86	| Skill | Runner (exists) | Fixtures file (new) |
87	|---|---|---|
88	| researcher | `skills/researcher.py` | `prompt-lab/fixtures/researcher_test_topics.json` |
89	| ideation | `skills/ideation.py` | `prompt-lab/fixtures/ideation_test_topics.json` |
90	| hook | `skills/hook.py` | `prompt-lab/fixtures/hook_test_topics.json` |
91	| outline | `skills/outline.py` | `prompt-lab/fixtures/outline_test_topics.json` |
92	| title | `skills/title.py` | `prompt-lab/fixtures/title_test_topics.json` |
93	| cascade | `skills/cascade.py` | `prompt-lab/fixtures/cascade_test_topics.json` |
94	| short_form | `skills/short_form.py` | `prompt-lab/fixtures/short_form_test_topics.json` |
95	| voice_cleanup | `skills/voice_cleanup.py` | `prompt-lab/fixtures/voice_cleanup_test_topics.json` |
96	
97	**Sample contents of `hook_test_topics.json`:**
98	```json
99	{
100	  "topics": [
101	    {"topic": "Rust async fundamentals", "audience": "intermediate devs", "platform": "youtube"},
102	    {"topic": "Vector databases for RAG", "audience": "AI engineers", "platform": "youtube"},
103	    {"topic": "Claude Code skills system", "audience": "Claude users", "platform": "youtube"},
104	    {"topic": "GPU acceleration on Windows", "audience": "ML researchers", "platform": "youtube"},
105	    {"topic": "Local-first dev workflow", "audience": "senior devs", "platform": "youtube"}
106	  ],
107	  "model_settings": {"model": "claude-sonnet-4-6", "temperature": 0.7, "max_tokens": 2000}
108	}
109	```
110	
111	**Why those exact contents:** every iteration runs the **same 5 topics** through **the same model settings**. Only the prompt changes. That's what makes score deltas comparable.
112	
113	**Status:** 8 fixtures files new. All 8 skill runners already exist, unchanged.
114	
115	---
116	
117	### 3.3 Karpathy's `val_bpb` metric  →  our `prompt-lab/scorers/<skill>_scorer.py`
118	
119	**Karpathy's version:** validation bits-per-byte — a single floating-point number. Lower is better.
120	
121	**Our version:** Python function that ingests skill output, returns **one floating-point number**. Higher is better.
122	
123	**Applies to all 8 skills.** Each gets its own scorer file with a skill-specific formula:
124	
125	| Scorer file (new) | Formula |
126	|---|---|
127	| `hook_scorer.py` | LLM-judge avg(scroll_stop, curiosity_gap, payoff) across 5 hooks |
128	| `outline_scorer.py` | programmatic (6 stages present, durations sum) + LLM-judge talking-point specificity |
129	| `title_scorer.py` | head-to-head LLM-judge win-rate vs. `skills/data/competitor_titles.json` |
130	| `voice_cleanup_scorer.py` | **programmatic**: `−banned_phrase_count + 0.5 × LLM-judge(voice_fidelity)`. Most trustworthy scorer — banned-phrase count is an exact integer. |
131	| `researcher_scorer.py` | LLM-judge: brief contains primary sources? gap analysis present? |
132	| `ideation_scorer.py` | LLM-judge: 9 distinct ideas? gap reasoning per idea? audience desire mapped? |
133	| `cascade_scorer.py` | LLM-judge per artifact (blog, twitter, linkedin) — composite |
134	| `short_form_scorer.py` | LLM-judge: 3 length variants present? hook-payoff intact at 30s/60s/90s? |
135	
136	**Pseudocode of `hook_scorer.py`:**
137	```python
138	def score_hook_output(generated_hooks: list[str]) -> float:
139	    scores = []
140	    for hook in generated_hooks:
141	        judge = llm_judge(
142	            hook=hook,
143	            rubric="Score 0-10 on each axis: scroll_stop, curiosity_gap, payoff_promise"
144	        )
145	        scores.append(mean([judge.scroll_stop, judge.curiosity_gap, judge.payoff]))
146	    return mean(scores)  # average across all 5 hooks
147	```
148	
149	**Status:** 8 scorer files new.
150	
151	---
152	
153	### 3.4 Karpathy's `program.md`  →  our `Content-Hub-Vault-V2/00-Management-V2/brief.md`
154	
155	**Karpathy's version:** human-authored markdown read by the agent before each session. Shapes what to optimize that night. Edited *before bedtime*.
156	
157	**Our version:** human-authored markdown read by `/prompt-lab` before each session. Same idea. **This IS Opportunity 3 in the survey below.**
158	
159	> **IMPORTANT — this file does NOT exist in your vault today.** You won't find it if you look. Confirmed when the repo was scanned on 2026-05-28: *"No `brief.md` or per-run instruction files found."*
160	>
161	> The path `Content-Hub-Vault-V2/00-Management-V2/brief.md` is the **proposed location** where this file *would* live. It gets **created when Opportunity 3 is built**. You'd write it once, then overwrite it each night before kicking off a new `/prompt-lab` run.
162	
163	**Sample contents (for a hook-optimization night):**
164	```markdown
165	# /prompt-lab brief — 2026-06-01
166	
167	Target file: prompts/hook.md
168	Optimize for: scroll-stop strength (weight 1.5x) + curiosity-gap (weight 1x)
169	De-prioritize: payoff-promise (already strong, weight 0.5x)
170	Constraints:
171	  - hooks must stay under 30 seconds spoken
172	  - banned: clickbait that doesn't deliver on the topic
173	Stopping condition: 8 hours OR no improvement for 20 iterations
174	```
175	
176	**Status:** new file — does not exist yet, would live at the path above once built.
177	
178	---
179	
180	### 3.5 Bonus — Karpathy's `results.tsv`  →  our `pipeline_results.tsv`
181	
182	Karpathy also has a `results.tsv` that logs every iteration. We need the same thing. **This IS Opportunity 2 in the survey below.**
183	
184	> **Same situation as `brief.md` — this file does NOT exist in your vault today.** It gets created when Opportunity 2 is built. The proposed path is `Content-Hub-Vault-V2/00-Management-V2/pipeline_results.tsv`.
185	
186	**Sample contents (from a hook night):**
187	```
188	timestamp              | prompt   | iter | composite | scroll | curiosity | payoff | kept
189	2026-06-01T22:15:03Z   | hook.md  | 1    | 7.20      | 7.2    | 6.5       | 8.0    | YES (baseline)
190	2026-06-01T22:20:11Z   | hook.md  | 2    | 6.83      | 5.8    | 7.0       | 7.5    | NO (reverted)
191	2026-06-01T22:25:45Z   | hook.md  | 3    | 7.85      | 8.1    | 7.2       | 8.2    | YES (new winner)
192	2026-06-01T22:30:22Z   | hook.md  | 4    | 7.40      | 7.5    | 7.0       | 7.8    | NO (reverted)
193	```
194	
195	Append-only. One row per iteration. Wake up, scan this file, see what improved.
196	
197	**Status:** new file — does not exist yet.
198	
199	---
200	
201	### 3.6 File Inventory — Side-by-Side
202	
203	| Karpathy's repo | Content Hub V2 equivalent | Status |
204	|---|---|---|
205	| `train.py` (mutable code) | `prompts/<skill>.md` × 8 | exists |
206	| `prepare.py` (fixed env) | `prompt-lab/fixtures/<skill>_test_topics.json` + `skills/<skill>.py` | 8 fixtures new, runners exist |
207	| `val_bpb` (the metric) | `prompt-lab/scorers/<skill>_scorer.py` × 8 | 8 new |
208	| `program.md` (rulebook) | `Content-Hub-Vault-V2/00-Management-V2/brief.md` | new = **Opp 3** |
209	| `results.tsv` (log) | `Content-Hub-Vault-V2/00-Management-V2/pipeline_results.tsv` | new = **Opp 2** |
210	| the autoresearch loop itself | `prompt-lab/loop.py` | new = **Opp 1 core** |
211	
212	**Net new code:** 8 fixtures + 8 scorers + 1 brief + 1 results file + 1 orchestrator = **19 new files**. All 16 existing files (8 prompts + 8 runners) reused untouched.
213	
214	---
215	
216	## 4. What Content Hub V2 Looks Like Today (Facts)
217	
218	From scanning the repo on 2026-05-28:
219	
220	| Component | Today |
221	|---|---|
222	| Prompts | **10 files** in `prompts/` — researcher, ideation, hook, outline, title, cascade, short_form, voice_cleanup, research_followups, yt_pipeline |
223	| Pipeline scripts | **15 Python files** in `skills/` — including a working `pipeline.py` that runs all 9 steps end-to-end |
224	| Skills | **8 production skills** (researcher → voice-cleanup) + utility skills |
225	| Per-skill evals | Yes — `.claude/skills/*/iteration-1/eval-*/` has `metrics.json` per skill |
226	| Global results file | **None.** No `pipeline_results.tsv`, no cross-run comparison |
227	| Per-run instruction file | **None.** No `brief.md`. Pipeline config comes from CLI args + auto-detected vault files |
228	| Current sprint phase | Phase 7 webapp (launcher + E2E) — Phases 1-6 done and live |
229	
230	**Bottom line:** the engine runs. The measurement layer doesn't exist yet.
231	
232	---
233	
234	## 5. The 5 Opportunities
235	
236	### Opportunity 1 — `/prompt-lab` (Autonomous Prompt Optimizer) — HIGHEST VALUE
237	
238	**The pitch:** Point it at any prompt in `prompts/`, go to sleep, wake up to a measurably better prompt.
239	
240	**Facts:**
241	- All 10 prompts already exist as plain `.md` files — the "mutable file" is already there.
242	- Each skill is already callable from Python (`skills/*.py`), so the loop can run them headlessly.
243	- Per-skill evals already exist (`.claude/skills/<skill>/iteration-1/`) — scoring scaffolding is partially there.
244	
245	**Assumptions:**
246	- An LLM-judge scoring rubric can produce stable, comparable scores across runs. *(Plausible — standard practice — but needs validation. A wobbly judge ruins the whole loop.)*
247	- Optimizing one prompt won't break the next stage downstream. *(Risk — mitigated by the final integration pass in §7.)*
248	
249	**Effort:** Medium. Reuses existing per-skill eval harness.
250	**Value:** **Highest.** Every downstream output gets better. Pays off forever.
251	
252	---
253	
254	### Opportunity 2 — `pipeline_results.tsv` (Lightweight Tracking Layer)
255	
256	**The pitch:** A single spreadsheet-style file that records every pipeline run so you can compare them.
257	
258	**Facts:**
259	- No such file exists today (confirmed).
260	- `pipeline.py` already has natural hook points where logging could be added.
261	- Direct port of autoresearch's `results.tsv`.
262	
263	**Assumptions:**
264	- A simple TSV is enough; no SQLite/Postgres needed yet. *(Probably true at current scale.)*
265	
266	**Effort:** Low. ~50 lines added to `pipeline.py` + a TSV file.
267	**Value:** Medium alone — high as a prerequisite. **Opportunity 1 needs this** to track variant scores.
268	
269	---
270	
271	### Opportunity 3 — `brief.md` (Per-Run Instruction File)
272	
273	**The pitch:** Write a one-page brief before bed; the whole pipeline reads it and shapes every decision around it.
274	
275	**Facts:**
276	- No per-run instruction file exists today.
277	- Direct port of autoresearch's `program.md`.
278	
279	**Assumptions:**
280	- You actually want to write a brief before each run. *(Worth confirming — if you prefer CLI flags, this is just extra ceremony.)*
281	- Skills can be modified to read it without major refactor. *(Likely — most skills already accept a research-brief file path.)*
282	
283	**Effort:** Low-medium. New file convention + small read in each of 8 skills.
284	**Value:** Medium. Biggest payoff combined with Opportunity 5.
285	
286	---
287	
288	### Opportunity 4 — Formalize Fixed Budgets as Logged "Experiment Parameters"
289	
290	**The pitch:** You already have hard limits (9 ideas, 5 hooks). Log them so you can see which limits worked.
291	
292	**Facts:**
293	- Skills already enforce hard counts (confirmed: ideation = 9, hook = 5, short_form = 3 lengths).
294	- Researcher has a query budget already partially enforced.
295	
296	**Assumptions:**
297	- These numbers are worth experimenting with at all. *(Maybe not — Kallaway-trained numbers may be locked-in by the methodology.)*
298	
299	**Effort:** Trivial. A few extra columns in the TSV from Opportunity 2.
300	**Value:** Low until you tweak the numbers. Cheap insurance.
301	
302	---
303	
304	### Opportunity 5 — `/pipeline-loop` (Overnight Autonomous Content Run)
305	
306	**The pitch:** Extend `/run-pipeline` with a quality gate — if a stage scores below threshold, retry with a different angle, automatically.
307	
308	**Facts:**
309	- `/run-pipeline` already exists and runs the full chain autonomously.
310	- It does NOT currently have a quality gate or retry loop.
311	
312	**Assumptions:**
313	- Stage-level quality scoring is reliable enough to drive retry decisions. *(Same risk as Opp 1.)*
314	- "Retry with different angle" can be implemented without prompt babysitting. *(Unclear — needs a controlled experiment.)*
315	
316	**Effort:** High. Depends on Opps 1, 2, 3 being solid first.
317	**Value:** Very high if it works. Most fragile of the five.
318	
319	---
320	
321	## 6. Recommended Build Order
322	
323	1. **Opportunity 2** (`pipeline_results.tsv`) — cheap, unlocks everything else.
324	2. **Opportunity 1** (`/prompt-lab`) — highest standalone ROI.
325	3. **Opportunity 3** (`brief.md`) — small lift, opens door to Opp 5.
326	4. **Opportunity 4** (logged budgets) — falls out of Opp 2 for free.
327	5. **Opportunity 5** (`/pipeline-loop`) — only after 1-4 prove the scoring layer is trustworthy.
328	
329	---
330	
331	## 7. Run Architecture — Locked Decision
332	
333	**Per-prompt, one at a time, in pipeline order. Then ONE final integration pass.**
334	
335	This matches Karpathy's own approach (he optimizes `train.py` with `prepare.py` frozen — never tries to optimize the whole stack at once).
336	
337	**The 9-night schedule:**
338	
339	| Night | Target prompt |
340	|---|---|
341	| 1 | `prompts/researcher.md` |
342	| 2 | `prompts/ideation.md` |
343	| 3 | `prompts/hook.md` |
344	| 4 | `prompts/outline.md` |
345	| 5 | `prompts/title.md` |
346	| 6 | `prompts/cascade.md` |
347	| 7 | `prompts/short_form.md` |
348	| 8 | `prompts/voice_cleanup.md` |
349	| 9 | Full-pipeline integration pass — revert any per-prompt change that broke the chain |
350	
351	Each night: ~5 min per iteration × ~8 hours = ~96 prompt variants tested. Winner committed to git, losers reverted.
352	
353	**Why per-prompt wins:**
354	- Fast loop (~5 min vs. 30+ min for end-to-end).
355	- Easy to debug — you know exactly which prompt change caused which score delta.
356	- Cheap to revert — if Night 3's hook prompt is worse, roll back that one file.
357	
358	**One-command convenience:** `/prompt-lab --all` could orchestrate all 9 nights automatically while keeping the per-prompt architecture underneath. UX wrapper, same architecture.
359	
360	---
361	
362	## 8. What You'll Notice After All 5 Are Built
363	
364	Stage-by-stage, with the **exact scoring metric** for each and which **Opportunities** drive each gain. Honest answer: real improvement, but not magic.
365	
366	| Stage | Today | After all 5 | Scoring metric (the actual number) | Opportunities involved | Realistic gain |
367	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
368	| **Hooks** | First-draft prompt — sometimes punchy, sometimes mid | Hook prompt tuned against Kallaway rubric. Duds drop out. | **Kallaway 3-axis LLM-judge (0-10 each):** scroll-stop, curiosity-gap, payoff promise. Composite = avg. | Opp 1, Opp 2 | 10-30% more hooks pass the scroll-stop bar |
369	| **Outlines** | Dopamine Ladder followed; pacing varies | Consistently hits all 6 stages with tighter talking points | **Mix: programmatic + LLM-judge.** Programmatic: all 6 stages? durations sum? Talking-point count in range? LLM-judge: specificity 0-10. | Opp 1, Opp 2, Opp 4 | ~20% less padding |
370	| **Titles** | 10 candidates, hit rate varies | Title prompt rewards titles that beat competitor benchmarks | **Head-to-head LLM-judge vs. `skills/data/competitor_titles.json`.** Score = win-rate %. | Opp 1, Opp 2 | More usable winners per batch |
371	| **Voice cleanup** | Removes banned phrases; still reads AI-ish | AI-ism count near-zero, tone markers preserved | (a) **Banned-phrase count from `prompts/voice_cleanup.md` list — exact integer, programmatic, the most trustworthy metric in the system.** (b) LLM-judge: voice fidelity 0-10. | Opp 1, Opp 2 | Noticeably less robotic |
372	| **Cross-pipeline** | One dud stage = manual re-run | Quality gate auto-retries duds with different angle | **Per-stage threshold** (each ≥ 7/10) + **final integration LLM-judge** 0-10. Below threshold → retry stage. | Opp 2, Opp 3, Opp 5 | Way less hand-holding |
373	
374	**All 5 Opportunities are covered by this table** — viewed from the outcome side:
375	- **Opp 1** drives 4 of 5 rows (hook, outline, title, voice).
376	- **Opp 2** is invisible but required by every row.
377	- **Opp 3** powers the cross-pipeline retry steering.
378	- **Opp 4** shows up in the outlines row (logged stage budgets).
379	- **Opp 5** = the cross-pipeline row entirely.
380	
381	**Compounded effect:** A 15% better hook + 15% better outline + 15% better voice ≠ 45%, but the final video feels meaningfully sharper than today's first-draft pipeline.
382	
383	**The honest ceiling:** Quality lift is **capped by the scorer**. If your LLM-judge gives noisy scores, you'll plateau fast — maybe 10% instead of 30%. The only way past that is feeding **real audience signal** (view-through rate, retention, CTR) into the loop. That's a v2 of the v2.
384	
385	**What you will NOT get:** 2x quality, viral guarantees, or a system that removes your judgment. You're still the final taste tester. The robot just stops handing you obvious duds.
386	
387	---
388	
389	## 9. What I'm NOT Recommending
390	
391	- **Don't port the ML training code.** autoresearch's `torch`/GPU/`train.py` parts are irrelevant — you're not training models.
392	- **Don't build the scorer last.** The whole pattern lives or dies on whether the score is trustworthy. Noisy scorer = theater.
393	- **Don't start with Opportunity 5.** Most fragile. Earn it after 1-4.
394	
395	---
396	
397	## 10. Critical Files Referenced
398	
399	| Path | Why it matters |
400	|---|---|
401	| `prompts/*.md` (8 production prompts) | The "mutable files" — what `/prompt-lab` rewrites each iteration |
402	| `skills/*.py` (8 skill runners) | The "ovens" — fixed, reused as-is, called by the loop |
403	| `skills/pipeline.py` | Natural insertion point for `pipeline_results.tsv` logging |
404	| `skills/data/competitor_titles.json` | Reference data for `title_scorer.py` head-to-head comparison |
405	| `.claude/skills/*/iteration-1/eval-*/metrics.json` | Existing per-skill eval scaffolding to reuse |
406	| (new) `Content-Hub-Vault-V2/00-Management-V2/brief.md` | Per-run rulebook (Opp 3) — does not exist yet |
407	| (new) `Content-Hub-Vault-V2/00-Management-V2/pipeline_results.tsv` | Append-only iteration log (Opp 2) — does not exist yet |
408	| (new) `prompt-lab/fixtures/<skill>_test_topics.json` × 8 | Fixed inputs per skill |
409	| (new) `prompt-lab/scorers/<skill>_scorer.py` × 8 | Per-skill scoring functions |
410	| (new) `prompt-lab/loop.py` | The autoresearch loop itself |
411	
412	---
413	
414	## 11. Open Questions
415	
416	1. **Do you trust LLM-as-judge scoring for hook/script quality?** If no, Opps 1 and 5 are dead in the water — we'd need a different scoring source (human ratings? real engagement data?).
417	2. **Is the existing per-skill eval scaffolding (`.claude/skills/*/iteration-1/`) something you actively use, or stale?** Determines whether `/prompt-lab` reuses it or starts fresh.
418	3. **Is `brief.md`-style per-run instruction something you'd actually write each night?** Or do you prefer ad-hoc CLI flags?

# The Self-Improvement Loop

**Where Can We Use Karpathy's `autoresearch` Pattern in Content Hub V2?**

**Type:** Opportunity survey (no implementation, no timing commitment)
**Date:** 2026-05-28
**Related:** [[Local_First_Skill_Engine_Plan]], [[Refined_Pipeline]], [[Researcher_Optimisation]]

---

## 1. Context — Why This Matters

Karpathy released a tiny open-source framework called `autoresearch`. The idea is dead simple:

> Let an AI agent **change one file**, **run a test**, **score the result**, then **keep the change or throw it away** — and repeat that loop overnight without you babysitting it.

He built it for ML training runs. But the **pattern itself** — *modify → score → keep-or-revert → repeat* — works anywhere you can measure quality.

Content Hub V2 has 10 prompts that were written once and never tested systematically. Every video script, hook, and title is generated by prompts nobody has measured. That's a huge improvement opportunity hiding in plain sight.

This document is a **survey** of 5 places autoresearch fits your system, with effort/value ratings, an honest "fact vs. assumption" split for each, and concrete file-by-file mapping.

---

## 2. How autoresearch Works (in 30 seconds, layman terms)

Imagine you have a recipe and a way to score the cake it produces (1-10 from a taste tester). autoresearch is the kitchen robot that:

1. Tweaks one ingredient in the recipe.
2. Bakes the cake (fixed time, fixed oven settings — same every run).
3. Scores it.
4. If the score went up, **keeps the tweak.** If it went down, **rips it out.**
5. Tweaks something else. Repeats all night.

In Karpathy's repo:
- **The recipe** = `train.py` (the only file the agent can touch)
- **The oven** = `prepare.py` (fixed — agent cannot change)
- **The taste tester** = a number called `val_bpb`
- **The rulebook** = `program.md` (you write this before bedtime: "tonight, optimize for X")

**Three things make the pattern work:** one mutable file, one fixed metric, one rulebook.

---

## 3. Karpathy's Four Files → Our Four Files (Direct Mapping)

The same four-file pattern, ported to Content Hub V2. Using `prompts/hook.md` as the running example — **the same shape applies to all 8 skills** (called out explicitly in each section).

---

### 3.1 Karpathy's `train.py`  →  our `prompts/<skill>.md`

**Karpathy's version:** PyTorch model + optimizer + training loop. The only file the agent is allowed to mutate.

**Our version:** the prompt markdown file. The only file `/prompt-lab` is allowed to mutate.

**Applies to all 8 skills:** [[researcher]], [[ideation]], [[hook]], [[outline]], [[title]], [[cascade]], [[short-form]], [[voice-cleanup]].

**Status:** all 8 files already exist on disk in `prompts/`.

**What's inside `prompts/hook.md` today (excerpt):**
> *"Generate 5 Kallaway hook variations using the 3-stage structure: scroll stop, curiosity gap, payoff promise. For each hook, produce a Spoken Line, a Visual Anchor, and a Curiosity Gap Marker..."*

**What `/prompt-lab` does to it each iteration:** rewrites sections, deletes lines, adds rules, restructures examples. Every variant gets a git commit. Bad variants → reverted. Good variants → kept and built on.

---

### 3.2 Karpathy's `prepare.py`  →  our `prompt-lab/fixtures/<skill>_test_topics.json` + existing `skills/<skill>.py`

**Karpathy's version:** loads dataset, sets constants (`MAX_SEQ_LEN`, `TIME_BUDGET`, `VOCAB_SIZE`). Fixed — agent cannot touch.

**Our version:** fixed test inputs + the skill runner. Two files together. Fixed — `/prompt-lab` cannot touch.

**Applies to all 8 skills.** Each gets its own fixtures file paired with its own existing runner:

| Skill | Runner (exists) | Fixtures file (new) |
|---|---|---|
| researcher | `skills/researcher.py` | `prompt-lab/fixtures/researcher_test_topics.json` |
| ideation | `skills/ideation.py` | `prompt-lab/fixtures/ideation_test_topics.json` |
| hook | `skills/hook.py` | `prompt-lab/fixtures/hook_test_topics.json` |
| outline | `skills/outline.py` | `prompt-lab/fixtures/outline_test_topics.json` |
| title | `skills/title.py` | `prompt-lab/fixtures/title_test_topics.json` |
| cascade | `skills/cascade.py` | `prompt-lab/fixtures/cascade_test_topics.json` |
| short_form | `skills/short_form.py` | `prompt-lab/fixtures/short_form_test_topics.json` |
| voice_cleanup | `skills/voice_cleanup.py` | `prompt-lab/fixtures/voice_cleanup_test_topics.json` |

**Sample contents of `hook_test_topics.json`:**
```json
{
  "topics": [
    {"topic": "Rust async fundamentals", "audience": "intermediate devs", "platform": "youtube"},
    {"topic": "Vector databases for RAG", "audience": "AI engineers", "platform": "youtube"},
    {"topic": "Claude Code skills system", "audience": "Claude users", "platform": "youtube"},
    {"topic": "GPU acceleration on Windows", "audience": "ML researchers", "platform": "youtube"},
    {"topic": "Local-first dev workflow", "audience": "senior devs", "platform": "youtube"}
  ],
  "model_settings": {"model": "claude-sonnet-4-6", "temperature": 0.7, "max_tokens": 2000}
}
```

**Why those exact contents:** every iteration runs the **same 5 topics** through **the same model settings**. Only the prompt changes. That's what makes score deltas comparable.

**Status:** 8 fixtures files new. All 8 skill runners already exist, unchanged.

---

### 3.3 Karpathy's `val_bpb` metric  →  our `prompt-lab/scorers/<skill>_scorer.py`

**Karpathy's version:** validation bits-per-byte — a single floating-point number. Lower is better.

**Our version:** Python function that ingests skill output, returns **one floating-point number**. Higher is better.

**Applies to all 8 skills.** Each gets its own scorer file with a skill-specific formula:

| Scorer file (new) | Formula |
|---|---|
| `hook_scorer.py` | LLM-judge avg(scroll_stop, curiosity_gap, payoff) across 5 hooks |
| `outline_scorer.py` | programmatic (6 stages present, durations sum) + LLM-judge talking-point specificity |
| `title_scorer.py` | head-to-head LLM-judge win-rate vs. `skills/data/competitor_titles.json` |
| `voice_cleanup_scorer.py` | **programmatic**: `−banned_phrase_count + 0.5 × LLM-judge(voice_fidelity)`. Most trustworthy scorer — banned-phrase count is an exact integer. |
| `researcher_scorer.py` | LLM-judge: brief contains primary sources? gap analysis present? |
| `ideation_scorer.py` | LLM-judge: 9 distinct ideas? gap reasoning per idea? audience desire mapped? |
| `cascade_scorer.py` | LLM-judge per artifact (blog, twitter, linkedin) — composite |
| `short_form_scorer.py` | LLM-judge: 3 length variants present? hook-payoff intact at 30s/60s/90s? |

**Pseudocode of `hook_scorer.py`:**
```python
def score_hook_output(generated_hooks: list[str]) -> float:
    scores = []
    for hook in generated_hooks:
        judge = llm_judge(
            hook=hook,
            rubric="Score 0-10 on each axis: scroll_stop, curiosity_gap, payoff_promise"
        )
        scores.append(mean([judge.scroll_stop, judge.curiosity_gap, judge.payoff]))
    return mean(scores)  # average across all 5 hooks
```

**Status:** 8 scorer files new.

---

### 3.4 Karpathy's `program.md`  →  our `Content-Hub-Vault-V2/00-Management-V2/brief.md`

**Karpathy's version:** human-authored markdown read by the agent before each session. Shapes what to optimize that night. Edited *before bedtime*.

**Our version:** human-authored markdown read by `/prompt-lab` before each session. Same idea. **This IS Opportunity 3 in the survey below.**

> **IMPORTANT — this file does NOT exist in your vault today.** You won't find it if you look. Confirmed when the repo was scanned on 2026-05-28: *"No `brief.md` or per-run instruction files found."*
>
> The path `Content-Hub-Vault-V2/00-Management-V2/brief.md` is the **proposed location** where this file *would* live. It gets **created when Opportunity 3 is built**. You'd write it once, then overwrite it each night before kicking off a new `/prompt-lab` run.

**Sample contents (for a hook-optimization night):**
```markdown

De-prioritize: payoff-promise (already strong, weight 0.5x)

  - banned: clickbait that doesn't deliver on the topic
Stopping condition: 8 hours OR no improvement for 20 iterations
```

**Status:** new file — does not exist yet, would live at the path above once built.

---

### 3.5 Bonus — Karpathy's `results.tsv`  →  our `pipeline_results.tsv`

Karpathy also has a `results.tsv` that logs every iteration. We need the same thing. **This IS Opportunity 2 in the survey below.**

> **Same situation as `brief.md` — this file does NOT exist in your vault today.** It gets created when Opportunity 2 is built. The proposed path is `Content-Hub-Vault-V2/00-Management-V2/pipeline_results.tsv`.

**Sample contents (from a hook night):**
```

2026-06-01T22:15:03Z   | hook.md  | 1    | 7.20      | 7.2    | 6.5       | 8.0    | YES (baseline)
2026-06-01T22:20:11Z   | hook.md  | 2    | 6.83      | 5.8    | 7.0       | 7.5    | NO (reverted)
2026-06-01T22:25:45Z   | hook.md  | 3    | 7.85      | 8.1    | 7.2       | 8.2    | YES (new winner)
2026-06-01T22:30:22Z   | hook.md  | 4    | 7.40      | 7.5    | 7.0       | 7.8    | NO (reverted)
```

Append-only. One row per iteration. Wake up, scan this file, see what improved.

**Status:** new file — does not exist yet.

---

### 3.6 File Inventory — Side-by-Side

| Karpathy's repo | Content Hub V2 equivalent | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `train.py` (mutable code) | `prompts/<skill>.md` × 8 | exists |
| `prepare.py` (fixed env) | `prompt-lab/fixtures/<skill>_test_topics.json` + `skills/<skill>.py` | 8 fixtures new, runners exist |
| `val_bpb` (the metric) | `prompt-lab/scorers/<skill>_scorer.py` × 8 | 8 new |
| `program.md` (rulebook) | `Content-Hub-Vault-V2/00-Management-V2/brief.md` | new = **Opp 3** |
| `results.tsv` (log) | `Content-Hub-Vault-V2/00-Management-V2/pipeline_results.tsv` | new = **Opp 2** |
| the autoresearch loop itself | `prompt-lab/loop.py` | new = **Opp 1 core** |

**Net new code:** 8 fixtures + 8 scorers + 1 brief + 1 results file + 1 orchestrator = **19 new files**. All 16 existing files (8 prompts + 8 runners) reused untouched.

---

## 4. What Content Hub V2 Looks Like Today (Facts)

From scanning the repo on 2026-05-28:

| Component | Today |
|---|---|
| Prompts | **10 files** in `prompts/` — researcher, ideation, hook, outline, title, cascade, short_form, voice_cleanup, research_followups, yt_pipeline |
| Pipeline scripts | **15 Python files** in `skills/` — including a working `pipeline.py` that runs all 9 steps end-to-end |
| Skills | **8 production skills** (researcher → voice-cleanup) + utility skills |
| Per-skill evals | Yes — `.claude/skills/*/iteration-1/eval-*/` has `metrics.json` per skill |
| Global results file | **None.** No `pipeline_results.tsv`, no cross-run comparison |
| Per-run instruction file | **None.** No `brief.md`. Pipeline config comes from CLI args + auto-detected vault files |
| Current sprint phase | Phase 7 webapp (launcher + E2E) — Phases 1-6 done and live |

**Bottom line:** the engine runs. The measurement layer doesn't exist yet.

---

## 5. The 5 Opportunities

### Opportunity 1 — `/prompt-lab` (Autonomous Prompt Optimizer) — HIGHEST VALUE

**The pitch:** Point it at any prompt in `prompts/`, go to sleep, wake up to a measurably better prompt.

**Facts:**
- All 10 prompts already exist as plain `.md` files — the "mutable file" is already there.
- Each skill is already callable from Python (`skills/*.py`), so the loop can run them headlessly.
- Per-skill evals already exist (`.claude/skills/<skill>/iteration-1/`) — scoring scaffolding is partially there.

**Assumptions:**
- An LLM-judge scoring rubric can produce stable, comparable scores across runs. *(Plausible — standard practice — but needs validation. A wobbly judge ruins the whole loop.)*
- Optimizing one prompt won't break the next stage downstream. *(Risk — mitigated by the final integration pass in §7.)*

**Effort:** Medium. Reuses existing per-skill eval harness.
**Value:** **Highest.** Every downstream output gets better. Pays off forever.

---

### Opportunity 2 — `pipeline_results.tsv` (Lightweight Tracking Layer)

**The pitch:** A single spreadsheet-style file that records every pipeline run so you can compare them.

**Facts:**
- No such file exists today (confirmed).
- `pipeline.py` already has natural hook points where logging could be added.
- Direct port of autoresearch's `results.tsv`.

**Assumptions:**
- A simple TSV is enough; no SQLite/Postgres needed yet. *(Probably true at current scale.)*

**Effort:** Low. ~50 lines added to `pipeline.py` + a TSV file.
**Value:** Medium alone — high as a prerequisite. **Opportunity 1 needs this** to track variant scores.

---

### Opportunity 3 — `brief.md` (Per-Run Instruction File)

**The pitch:** Write a one-page brief before bed; the whole pipeline reads it and shapes every decision around it.

**Facts:**
- No per-run instruction file exists today.
- Direct port of autoresearch's `program.md`.

**Assumptions:**
- You actually want to write a brief before each run. *(Worth confirming — if you prefer CLI flags, this is just extra ceremony.)*
- Skills can be modified to read it without major refactor. *(Likely — most skills already accept a research-brief file path.)*

**Effort:** Low-medium. New file convention + small read in each of 8 skills.
**Value:** Medium. Biggest payoff combined with Opportunity 5.

---

### Opportunity 4 — Formalize Fixed Budgets as Logged "Experiment Parameters"

**The pitch:** You already have hard limits (9 ideas, 5 hooks). Log them so you can see which limits worked.

**Facts:**
- Skills already enforce hard counts (confirmed: ideation = 9, hook = 5, short_form = 3 lengths).
- Researcher has a query budget already partially enforced.

**Assumptions:**
- These numbers are worth experimenting with at all. *(Maybe not — Kallaway-trained numbers may be locked-in by the methodology.)*

**Effort:** Trivial. A few extra columns in the TSV from Opportunity 2.
**Value:** Low until you tweak the numbers. Cheap insurance.

---

### Opportunity 5 — `/pipeline-loop` (Overnight Autonomous Content Run)

**The pitch:** Extend `/run-pipeline` with a quality gate — if a stage scores below threshold, retry with a different angle, automatically.

**Facts:**
- `/run-pipeline` already exists and runs the full chain autonomously.
- It does NOT currently have a quality gate or retry loop.

**Assumptions:**
- Stage-level quality scoring is reliable enough to drive retry decisions. *(Same risk as Opp 1.)*
- "Retry with different angle" can be implemented without prompt babysitting. *(Unclear — needs a controlled experiment.)*

**Effort:** High. Depends on Opps 1, 2, 3 being solid first.
**Value:** Very high if it works. Most fragile of the five.

---

## 6. Recommended Build Order

1. **Opportunity 2** (`pipeline_results.tsv`) — cheap, unlocks everything else.
2. **Opportunity 1** (`/prompt-lab`) — highest standalone ROI.
3. **Opportunity 3** (`brief.md`) — small lift, opens door to Opp 5.
4. **Opportunity 4** (logged budgets) — falls out of Opp 2 for free.
5. **Opportunity 5** (`/pipeline-loop`) — only after 1-4 prove the scoring layer is trustworthy.

---

## 7. Run Architecture — Locked Decision

**Per-prompt, one at a time, in pipeline order. Then ONE final integration pass.**

This matches Karpathy's own approach (he optimizes `train.py` with `prepare.py` frozen — never tries to optimize the whole stack at once).

**The 9-night schedule:**

| Night | Target prompt |
|---|---|
| 1 | `prompts/researcher.md` |
| 2 | `prompts/ideation.md` |
| 3 | `prompts/hook.md` |
| 4 | `prompts/outline.md` |
| 5 | `prompts/title.md` |
| 6 | `prompts/cascade.md` |
| 7 | `prompts/short_form.md` |
| 8 | `prompts/voice_cleanup.md` |
| 9 | Full-pipeline integration pass — revert any per-prompt change that broke the chain |

Each night: ~5 min per iteration × ~8 hours = ~96 prompt variants tested. Winner committed to git, losers reverted.

**Why per-prompt wins:**
- Fast loop (~5 min vs. 30+ min for end-to-end).
- Easy to debug — you know exactly which prompt change caused which score delta.
- Cheap to revert — if Night 3's hook prompt is worse, roll back that one file.

**One-command convenience:** `/prompt-lab --all` could orchestrate all 9 nights automatically while keeping the per-prompt architecture underneath. UX wrapper, same architecture.

---

## 8. What You'll Notice After All 5 Are Built

Stage-by-stage, with the **exact scoring metric** for each and which **Opportunities** drive each gain. Honest answer: real improvement, but not magic.

| Stage | Today | After all 5 | Scoring metric (the actual number) | Opportunities involved | Realistic gain |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Hooks** | First-draft prompt — sometimes punchy, sometimes mid | Hook prompt tuned against Kallaway rubric. Duds drop out. | **Kallaway 3-axis LLM-judge (0-10 each):** scroll-stop, curiosity-gap, payoff promise. Composite = avg. | Opp 1, Opp 2 | 10-30% more hooks pass the scroll-stop bar |
| **Outlines** | Dopamine Ladder followed; pacing varies | Consistently hits all 6 stages with tighter talking points | **Mix: programmatic + LLM-judge.** Programmatic: all 6 stages? durations sum? Talking-point count in range? LLM-judge: specificity 0-10. | Opp 1, Opp 2, Opp 4 | ~20% less padding |
| **Titles** | 10 candidates, hit rate varies | Title prompt rewards titles that beat competitor benchmarks | **Head-to-head LLM-judge vs. `skills/data/competitor_titles.json`.** Score = win-rate %. | Opp 1, Opp 2 | More usable winners per batch |
| **Voice cleanup** | Removes banned phrases; still reads AI-ish | AI-ism count near-zero, tone markers preserved | (a) **Banned-phrase count from `prompts/voice_cleanup.md` list — exact integer, programmatic, the most trustworthy metric in the system.** (b) LLM-judge: voice fidelity 0-10. | Opp 1, Opp 2 | Noticeably less robotic |
| **Cross-pipeline** | One dud stage = manual re-run | Quality gate auto-retries duds with different angle | **Per-stage threshold** (each ≥ 7/10) + **final integration LLM-judge** 0-10. Below threshold → retry stage. | Opp 2, Opp 3, Opp 5 | Way less hand-holding |

**All 5 Opportunities are covered by this table** — viewed from the outcome side:
- **Opp 1** drives 4 of 5 rows (hook, outline, title, voice).
- **Opp 2** is invisible but required by every row.
- **Opp 3** powers the cross-pipeline retry steering.
- **Opp 4** shows up in the outlines row (logged stage budgets).
- **Opp 5** = the cross-pipeline row entirely.

**Compounded effect:** A 15% better hook + 15% better outline + 15% better voice ≠ 45%, but the final video feels meaningfully sharper than today's first-draft pipeline.

**The honest ceiling:** Quality lift is **capped by the scorer**. If your LLM-judge gives noisy scores, you'll plateau fast — maybe 10% instead of 30%. The only way past that is feeding **real audience signal** (view-through rate, retention, CTR) into the loop. That's a v2 of the v2.

**What you will NOT get:** 2x quality, viral guarantees, or a system that removes your judgment. You're still the final taste tester. The robot just stops handing you obvious duds.

---

## 9. What I'm NOT Recommending

- **Don't port the ML training code.** autoresearch's `torch`/GPU/`train.py` parts are irrelevant — you're not training models.
- **Don't build the scorer last.** The whole pattern lives or dies on whether the score is trustworthy. Noisy scorer = theater.
- **Don't start with Opportunity 5.** Most fragile. Earn it after 1-4.

---

## 10. Critical Files Referenced

| Path | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| `prompts/*.md` (8 production prompts) | The "mutable files" — what `/prompt-lab` rewrites each iteration |
| `skills/*.py` (8 skill runners) | The "ovens" — fixed, reused as-is, called by the loop |
| `skills/pipeline.py` | Natural insertion point for `pipeline_results.tsv` logging |
| `skills/data/competitor_titles.json` | Reference data for `title_scorer.py` head-to-head comparison |
| `.claude/skills/*/iteration-1/eval-*/metrics.json` | Existing per-skill eval scaffolding to reuse |
| (new) `Content-Hub-Vault-V2/00-Management-V2/brief.md` | Per-run rulebook (Opp 3) — does not exist yet |
| (new) `Content-Hub-Vault-V2/00-Management-V2/pipeline_results.tsv` | Append-only iteration log (Opp 2) — does not exist yet |
| (new) `prompt-lab/fixtures/<skill>_test_topics.json` × 8 | Fixed inputs per skill |
| (new) `prompt-lab/scorers/<skill>_scorer.py` × 8 | Per-skill scoring functions |
| (new) `prompt-lab/loop.py` | The autoresearch loop itself |

---

## 11. Open Questions

1. **Do you trust LLM-as-judge scoring for hook/script quality?** If no, Opps 1 and 5 are dead in the water — we'd need a different scoring source (human ratings? real engagement data?).
2. **Is the existing per-skill eval scaffolding (`.claude/skills/*/iteration-1/`) something you actively use, or stale?** Determines whether `/prompt-lab` reuses it or starts fresh.
3. **Is `brief.md`-style per-run instruction something you'd actually write each night?** Or do you prefer ad-hoc CLI flags?

---

**References:** [[reference-autoresearch]] · [[Local_First_Skill_Engine_Plan]] · [[Refined_Pipeline]] · [[Researcher_Optimisation]]
